undocumented.title: Default nationality is 'gb' (Great Britain)
undocumented.code_does: When no nationality is supplied the procedure defaults to 'gb'; the spec only says 'a default nationality shall be applied' without specifying which one.
undocumented.why_it_matters: Callers relying on spec alone cannot predict the language/locale of generated names for the default case.

undocumented.title: Names fetched from external HTTP API (randomuser.me)
undocumented.code_does: Each iteration issues an HTTP GET to https://randomuser.me/api/?nat=<Nationality> and parses the JSON response for first name, last name, and gender.
undocumented.why_it_matters: Network availability and third-party API uptime become a hard dependency; no spec rule mentions this external dependency.

undocumented.title: SEX field populated from API gender response
undocumented.code_does: The employee SEX column is set to the first character of the 'gender' field returned by the randomuser.me API (e.g. 'm' or 'f').
undocumented.why_it_matters: Gender assignment is undocumented in any spec rule; the field's derivation and valid values are not specified.

undocumented.title: MIDINIT derived as first character of first name
undocumented.code_does: The MIDINIT (middle initial) column is set to substr(first_name, 1, 1) — the first letter of the employee's first name, not a true middle initial.
undocumented.why_it_matters: No spec rule describes how MIDINIT is populated; using the first-name initial is semantically incorrect and could mislead downstream consumers.

undocumented.title: JOB column assigned a random hex-based code
undocumented.code_does: Each employee's JOB column is set to 'JOB' concatenated with 4 random hex characters (e.g. 'JOB3F9A').
undocumented.why_it_matters: No spec rule describes how the JOB field is populated; the format is undocumented.

undocumented.title: PHONENO generated as 4-char hex string into a CHAR(5) column
undocumented.code_does: Phone number is set to substr(HEX(rand()), 1, 4), producing a 4-character hex string, while the EMPLOYEE table defines PHONENO as CHAR(5) with a CHECK constraint requiring '00000'–'99998'.
undocumented.why_it_matters: Hex digits A–F do not satisfy the all-numeric CHECK constraint on PHONENO, which may cause insertion failures at runtime; this mismatch is undocumented.

undocumented.title: Education level upper bound is 19 (not 20)
undocumented.code_does: Ed level is computed as 12 + int(rand() * 8); since int(rand() * 8) yields 0–7, the maximum possible value is 19 inclusive, consistent with BR-061.
undocumented.why_it_matters: The expression int(rand()*8) never produces 8, so the value 20 is unreachable; this boundary detail is not captured in the spec.

undocumented.title: INSERT uses WITH NC (no-commit) isolation
undocumented.code_does: Each INSERT statement is executed with 'WITH NC' (no commitment control), meaning records are not written under transaction control.
undocumented.why_it_matters: Partial population runs cannot be rolled back on failure; this transactional behaviour is not documented in any spec rule.
